title: Permission Lanes: Workspace Role Journeys with Cost Impact & Rollout Lenses
creator: Priya Nair
description: Goal: Design a compact, scannable console surface that visualizes a user or role's access across multiple workspaces (the 'Permission Lane'), surfaces the cost and potential attack surface per role, and integrates rollout controls (canary/A-B) and audit-timeline context. This ticket covers low-fidelity -> interactive prototype, stakeholder reviews, and acceptance criteria for handoff to ENG for a v1 experimental rollout. The feature should help engineers and security reviewers quickly answer: 'Who has this permission, across which workspaces, what is the monthly token/compute cost exposure, and when was it last used/changed?'.
acceptance_criteria: A compact Permission Lane UI that lists a selected role or user and shows per-workspace access chips with color-coded risk (green/amber/red)
Inline cost estimator showing monthly token/compute estimate per workspace when role actions are used (sums to team-level cost)
Rollout lens: ability to attach a canary or A/B rollout to a role change with quick toggles and an inline explanation of fallback behavior
Audit timeline: show last N events (grants/revokes/role changes/auth events) with links to full audit entries
Prototype reachable in Figma with interactive variants and two defined states for mobile/desktop
Design tokens and component spec documented in the Console design system for chips, timeline rows, and cost pills
Edge-case: for cross-org admins the lane collapses into 'global view' with workspace toggles to avoid overload
prototype_iterations: v0 - sketches (2026-02-18): lane metaphor exploration, vertical timeline vs horizontal lanes
v1 - low-fidelity (2026-02-25): basic chips, cost pill, static timeline rows
v2 - interactive (2026-03-03): canary toggle, hover affordances, audit tooltips
v3 - handoff-ready (2026-03-11): component mapping and accessibility notes
usability_findings: Participants (n=6 security reviewers) confused the cost pill with billing quota; renamed to 'estimated compute cost'
Users wanted a one-click 'show recent failures' filter on the audit timeline
Mobile testers requested collapsing lanes into accordion rows; introduced compact lane variant
PM asked for clearer language around 'canary' to avoid accidental rollouts; added confirmation modal copy
review_feedback: Miguel Torres (ENG): prefers server-driven pagination for audit timeline, flagged potential performance concern for large orgs
Aisha Chen (PM): asked to include a linkage to cost centers and tagging metadata for finance review
Security team (J. Morales): request to highlight service accounts separately and offer 'suspend' action for high-risk roles
Design review (Team): accessibility pass required for color contrast on risk chips
next_steps: Incorporate ENG feedback on pagination and propose a hybrid client/server timeline (by 2026-03-16)
Update copy for canary confirmation and create content variants for different org roles (by 2026-03-18)
Export component tokens and submit Console design-system PR referencing component ids (by 2026-03-20)
Schedule a cross-functional demo with Security, PM, and ENG to align on rollout controls (week of 2026-03-22)
